objects.summary: P1 review finds gh api --paginate output is multiple JSON pages, while direct json.loads after naive replacement can raise Extra data; watchdog can fail entirely beyond 100 comments unless pages are slurped/flattened correctly.

P2 review finds A2 role identity is trusted from free-form comment headers without authenticating GitHub author identity, allowing third-party comments to spoof builder/orchestrator, inject waits or suppress reminders.

P2 review finds CLOS[id] keys only on the bare ID; later reuse of the same ID can make a new wait appear already closed. Closure must bind to original wait/comment identity or enforce global uniqueness.

P2 review finds publish-block output directories are reused without cleanup; stale block_N files can survive a later successful extraction and be accidentally republished. Output must be empty/atomic per run.

P1 scientific review finds B2's claimed shadow-read prohibition is violated if PricePanel.load materializes the entire CSV before restriction; causal invariant requires raw-row filtering before panel construction or a weaker explicitly stated no-derived-statistics claim.

cross_object_findings.finding: Even after first-order fixes, bounded inline reviews found pagination crashes, actor spoofing, closure-ID aliasing and stale-output contamination. These are decision-relevant counterexamples, not stylistic review churn.
Coordination automation must bind role-bearing statements to attested GitHub identities; a DE: header alone cannot grant routing authority.
Wait closure/dedupe keys must include the source object identity, not only a reusable human ID, or later work can be suppressed by historical state.
A claim of no shadow access is false if protected rows are materialized before later restriction. The access boundary must be enforced before parsing/materialization, not only before statistics.
